title: Grade 7 French — Mon, May 25
description: La routine quotidienne — Day 1 of 5: Les verbes en -ER et le vocabulaire de la routine
subject: french

questions.question: What is the infinitive ending for the most common French verb group?
questions.explanation: -ER verbs are the largest and most regular group in French. Examples: manger (to eat), parler (to speak), habiter (to live). They follow a predictable conjugation pattern.

questions.question: Conjugate 'manger' (to eat) for 'je':
questions.explanation: 'Je mange' = I eat. -ER verb rule: drop -ER, add endings: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent. 'Je mange, tu manges, il/elle mange, nous mangeons, vous mangez, ils/elles mangent.'

questions.question: What does 'se lever' mean in the context of daily routine?
options: to get up / to wake up and get out of bed
questions.explanation: 'Se lever' = to get up. It's a reflexive verb (se + verb). Daily routine: se lever (get up), se laver (wash), se brosser les dents (brush teeth), se coucher (go to bed).

questions.question: Which verb means 'to have breakfast' in French?
options: prendre le petit-déjeuner / prendre son petit-dej
questions.explanation: 'Prendre le petit-déjeuner' = to have breakfast. 'Déjeuner' = to have lunch. 'Dîner' = to have dinner. Breakfast is 'le petit-déjeuner' (the little lunch).

questions.question: Conjugate 'parler' for 'vous':
questions.explanation: 'Vous parlez' = you speak (formal/plural). -ER endings: je -e, tu -es, il -e, nous -ons, vous -ez, ils -ent. The 'vous' form always ends in -ez for -ER verbs.

questions.question: What does 'habiter' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Habiter' = to live somewhere. 'J'habite à Paris' = I live in Paris. Common -ER verb used to describe where someone lives.

questions.question: Complete: 'Le matin, je ___ (regarder) la télévision.'
questions.explanation: 'Je regarde la télévision' = I watch television. Drop -ER from 'regarder', add -e for 'je'. Simple -ER conjugation.

questions.question: Translate: 'She works at home.'
questions.explanation: 'Elle travaille à la maison.' 'Travailler' = to work. Note: -iller verbs conjugate as: je travaille, tu travailles, il/elle travaille (double-L in writing, but pronounce as single sound).

questions.question: What does 'rentrer à la maison' mean?
options: to come home / to return home
questions.explanation: 'Rentrer' = to come/go back. 'Rentrer à la maison' = to come home. Daily routine: je rentre à la maison à 17h = I come home at 5pm.

questions.question: Conjugate 'écouter' (to listen) for 'nous':
questions.explanation: 'Nous écoutons' = we listen. The 'nous' form of -ER verbs always ends in -ons: nous écoutons, nous parlons, nous mangeons. Pattern is very regular.

questions.question: Which -ER verb best completes: 'Le soir, je ___ mes devoirs.'
questions.explanation: 'Je prépare mes devoirs' = I do/prepare my homework. 'Préparer' = to prepare. Also common: 'faire les devoirs' (but 'faire' is irregular). 'Préparer' is -ER.

questions.question: What is the 'ils' form of 'aimer'?
questions.explanation: 'Ils aiment' = they love/like. -ER endings for ils/elles: always -ent. Note: 'aiment' is pronounced the same as 'aime' (the -ent ending is silent). 'Ils aiment la musique.'

questions.question: Translate: 'We eat dinner at 8 o'clock.'
questions.explanation: 'Nous dînons à 20 heures.' 'Dîner' = to have dinner. 20h = 8pm (French uses 24-hour clock formally). 'Nous dînons' = nous + -ons ending.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly describes a morning routine?
options: Le matin, je mange le petit-déjeuner et je regardes les nouvelles.
Le matin, je prends le petit-déjeuner et je regarde les nouvelles.
Le matin, j'ai petit-déjeuner et je regarde les nouvelles.
Le matin, je prend le petit-déjeuner et je regarde les nouvelles.
questions.explanation: 'Je prends le petit-déjeuner' (prendre = irregular, je prends) + 'je regarde les nouvelles' (regarder = -ER, je regarde). Option A has 'regardes' (wrong for je). Option C has 'j'ai' (wrong). Option D has 'prend' (wrong for je).

questions.question: List 4 common -ER verbs used in daily routine:
questions.explanation: manger (eat), parler (speak), habiter (live), travailler (work) are all regular -ER verbs common in daily routine descriptions. The other options are irregular verbs (-IR, irregular, or modal verbs).
